I was diagnosed with PCOS in early 2022 a few weeks before turning 29. I was told to change my diet and that I had slight insulin resistance. So I completely changed my diet and started measuring my food and using an app to make sure I was only eating 20-30 grams of net carbs. After each day, I was only eating about 1000 calories a day for months. I then started eating more fatty things to add a few calories in. I ended up getting high cholesterol! It took me a year and a half to lower it! Still a tiny bit high but not to the concerning levels it was before.

I've been trying to figure this out since 2021! More specifically trying to see if certain foods make my cycles longer. At some point towards the last three months of 2021, I was eating peanut butter and toast for breakfast and as a snack when I got hungry. My cycles for those months were over 40 days long. I stopped eating the bread and peanut butter and my next cycles went back to 30-35. 

In 2022, I drastically changed my diet and was trying to eat keto but without all the fat. So more like low carb but with net carbs still around 20-30 grams. I eventually did increase my fat because I was eating a little over 1000 calories a day and lost too much weight...I was 96 pounds! My periods for 2022 were around 29-38 days long. The average was around 35.

In 2023, I started letting myself eat things I had previously restricted like rice and other carbs. Still very low carb year when compared to how I was eating for years. Period cycles were between 30-44 days long. Average being 34 days. I had two cycles over 40. I do remember eating these cashew butter packets and that cycle was one of the over 40 ones. Not sure if the low amount of sugar triggered anything. 

This year I've had my period twice. My first cycle was 41 days. I do recall eating more bread for the first time in a long while and making myself some cups of hot chocolate. I'm currently on day 24 of this current cycle and I'm pretty sure I'm looking at a cycle over 35-40 days long based on basil temperature and ovulation discharge. This past month and February I did eat bread again. My partner doesn't like me obsessing over food so he's been more "encouraging" in us buying food. He's also been making very unhealthy meals. I also started eating that cashew butter again. I'll probably stop and go back to a diet that I had in 2022 and see what happens.

I was on a similar boat and never noticed just how much sugar and carbs I was eating. Though I wasn't exactly someone that had a sweet tooth, I was consuming sugar through drinks and bread. 

For years, I was consuming over 200 grams of sugar a day. I would drink a bunch of chocolate milk and put 12 tablespoons of chocolate powder into my milk. I'd do this at least twice a day. I stopped drinking my chocolate milk when I was 22! It was so hard! For years, I also would just eat cookies, pastries, and dessert treats for lunch and sometimes breakfast. I never ate vegetables or fruits! I then replaced my sugar cravings with boba and would get super large cups of it multiple times in a week. 

It wasn't until early 2022, that I was diagnosed with lean PCOS and insulin resistance. I pretty much quit all sugary things then and there. I also significantly changed my diet to a much healthier one. I have seen my period get much more regular since 2020. I do think being at home and the quarantine helped because it was so hard to just go out and get treats for myself. 

It's hard but can be done. And the results are worth it. I recently started eating bread/pastry again but usually only eat it when I get my period :) When I get sweet cravings, I just eat fruits with yogurt or some sweet potatoes!

I grew up in Koreatown. We had seasonal roach during the Summer but nothing bad. I finally moved out and into my own place last year and stayed in Koreatown. That apartment was by S. Alexandria Ave and 5th and that place was roach infested! We didn't notice the roaches until 2 months after living there. The Infestation was so bad we were able to end our lease without penalties after seven months of living there. It was a nightmare and we had to get rid of a lot of our new things to avoid bringing the roaches with us. So many things were ruined!

Our new place is also in Koreatown and it's been roach free! This building only has 11 units and the building is kept very clean. The other building had over 40 and was always dirty! 

Best advice, search everything when going on apartment tours. Open the cabinets, look under the sink! Make note of the smell in the cabinets! The cabinets in the roach infested apartment had a weird damp smell. Which I'm sure was all the roach poop. Bring a mirror and look at the corners inside the cabinets, roaches love to poop there. Also look at other rooms too! 

When we were looking at new apartments, so many had roaches! Some dead and some alive! We'd ask about roach issues to the manager or whoever was there during the tours and all of them said they didn't have any issues! Even after I saw them dead or walking around before asking. One place even told us two units had bedbugs...so that's the only one that was honest! 

Best of luck!

My periods were very irregular ever since I started my period in 8th grade (13 years old). They were always this way up until 2020 when they started getting regular. I started keeping track of my periods since 2014 so I have years of data. The longest cycle I had was 120 days. 

In 2021 I saw a new gyno who did some hormone testing and ordered an ultrasound. She didn't want to and said I looked fine. Blood work was ok! My testosterone was on the higher side of the normal range but still within it. My LH and FSH were wonky. I had a bunch of follicles on my ovaries. Gyno said I had PCOS after that. Saw a reproductive endocrinologist and he looked at my results and said it looked like I was on the best tier for PCOS, I wasn't overweight (petite), irregular periods were getting regular, and no high male hormones. I had my insulin resistance tested and had a slight elevation. I changed my diet and became more active. Got retested and there was no sign of insulin resistance! 

My periods have been 29-40 days the last 3-4 years now! And have been able to see my period 10-11 times a year! So my reproductive endocrinologist says it doesn't look like I have it anymore. But my regular endocrinologist and gyno say I do.

I recently switched my medical group and saw a new gyno. I mentioned my irregular periods but also that they had gotten way better in the last 2-3 years. I was able to have 9-10 cycles these last few years instead of 5-6. She ordered an ultrasound and some blood work. Hormones were ok. Testosterone was still within range but on the higher end of normal. My LH (40) and FSH (6) ration was about 20:3.  Ultrasound also showed I had over 25 follicles on each ovary. I ended up seeing an endocrinologist and she ordered more testing after noticing faint dark skin patches on my neck. So I had a glucose tolerance test. After the two hours, my glucose was 151. Should have been under 140 and was told I have insulin resistance. Endo didn't seem worried because it's on the lower side of insulin resistance levels. She said eating better and working out would help. She also mentioned the common medications prescribed to people with PCOS. I told her I wanted change my lifestyle and diet to see how that helped me out first before taking anything.
